title: Finite-order distribution algebra and tangent Lie algebra of a commutative bialgebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $C$ a commutative unital $k$-algebra equipped with unital algebra maps $\Delta:C\to C\otimes_k C$ and $\varepsilon:C\to k$ satisfying coassociativity and both counit identities, using the module tensor product [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and its algebra tensor-product structure [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Put $I=\ker\varepsilon$. In the full convolution algebra $C^*=\operatorname{Hom}_k(C,k)$ [lem-sfb-convolution-linear-map-algebra], define $\operatorname{HasDistributionOrder}(n,a)$ by $a(I^{n+1})=0$ for $n\in\mathbb N$, $F_n$ as this annihilator for nonnegative integral $n$, and $F_n=0$ for negative integral $n$. Define $\operatorname{Dist}(C)=\{a\in C^*: \exists n\in\mathbb N,\ a(I^{n+1})=0\}$ with the inherited unital $k$-subalgebra structure, product $(a*b)(c)=(a\otimes b)(\Delta c)$ and unit $\varepsilon$. Define $L(C)=\{v\in C^*:v(xy)=\varepsilon(x)v(y)+v(x)\varepsilon(y)\text{ for all }x,y\in C\}$ with the inherited Lie subalgebra structure [def-wf-lie-algebra] of the convolution commutator Lie algebra, $[v,w]=v*w-w*v$. The proof fields asserting closure of these carriers under the inherited operations are named auxiliary theorems; the carriers and every operation are the displayed real constructions. No antipode, finite generation, smoothness, cocommutativity or characteristic restriction is imposed.
